messages:
tiana: Heads up — the tutorial sampleapp fails for a customer when they rotate their org key. Error is 401 with 'invalid scopes' even though they set the new key in REDWOOD_API_KEY.
kevin: hmm, can you paste the exact env they used? org vs project keys matter here.
tiana: They used the default quickstart env:
```
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-org-abc123
export REDWOOD_PROJECT=acme-prod
```
Then rotated to sk-project-xyz and updated REDWOOD_API_KEY to that. App started throwing 401s after a minute with ongoing websocket streams breaking.
maria: That sounds like SDK parity bug — CLI and SDK have different precedence for org vs project-scoped keys. CLI treats REDWOOD_API_KEY as project when REDWOOD_PROJECT is set; SDK still prefers org-level token if it was previously cached.
sam: Repro steps would be helpful. Is there a cached token in ~/.redwood/creds or similar?
tiana: I dug in: sampleapp uses the JS SDK and also uses the CLI to bootstrap creds. Steps I used locally:
1) run `redwood login --org acme` (stores org token)
2) start sampleapp which reads process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY (unset locally so it falls back to cached credential)
3) rotate key in dashboard to project key and `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-project-xyz`
4) app logs: `401 invalid_scopes` after first request.
kevin: OK that's actionable. Looks like the SDK has caching + precedence bug: cache key lookup uses org-scoped token first, even if REDWOOD_API_KEY env var is present. Should be: env var override -> explicit CLI bootstrap -> cached fallback.
josh: I can reproduce with a tiny script, will post gist. Quick workaround: explicitly set REDWOOD_PROJECT_TOKEN or REDWOOD_PROJECT_API_KEY (new env we could document) or restart process to flush in-memory cache.
credentials-bot: Automated note: detected mention of env var conventions mismatch. Suggest filing a DX ticket.
maria: Proposal: SDK change to re-evaluate env var on `new Client()` and prefer any explicit env var over cached CLI creds. Also add a deprecation warning when both org and project tokens appear in cache. Add a small behavioral test in integration suite.
sam: Also update sampleapp quickstart to recommend using `REDWOOD_PROJECT_API_KEY` for project-scoped keys until parity is fixed. Add a short blurb about long-lived vs rotating keys and recommended rotation cadence.
tiana: +1. Also can we add a cred-lint in dev tools to catch when someone sets REDWOOD_API_KEY but also has a conflicting cached org token? Could warn during startup: `Warning: using cached org token; export REDWOOD_API_KEY to override`.
kevin: I'll open an SDK PR for the precedence fix and add a runtime warning. Assigning to me and @maria for tests/docs. Will add an optional env var `REDWOOD_CRED_PRECEDENCE=env,cli,cache` for advanced debugging.
tiana: thanks! Can we also add a small debug command to the CLI: `redwood creds info` that prints which token is active and its scopes? That would have prevented the support back-and-forth.
maria: good call, adding to the CLI backlog. For now I'll update the sampleapp README with a clear example: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-project-xyz && node app.js` and call out that rotation may require process restart until SDK patch lands.
josh: gist: https://gist.github.com/josh/aa1b2c3 — shows minimal repro with node fetch and stream kept open.
tiana: awesome — I'll ping the customer and give the workaround + ETA on SDK fix. :thumbsup:
